proof.text: Use HenselianLocalRing.TFAE to obtain monic simple-root lifting. Let x be the prime q' in Spec B and y its image in Spec S. The affine residue-field isomorphisms identify beta:B→kappa(x) and alpha:S→kappa(y). Naturality gives beta composed with phi equal to the scheme residue-field map composed with alpha. The given ideal residue-field bijection, composed with S→kappa(m), makes S→kappa(q') surjective; transport across the affine residue-field isomorphism makes beta composed with phi surjective. Thus the scheme residue-field map is surjective, and it is injective because it is a homomorphism of fields.

Apply the already proved root-lifting retraction theorem with phi.toAlgebra, this root-lifting property, and the converted residue-field bijection. Both given algebra maps have maximal-ideal preimage q', so uniqueness identifies each with the unique retraction, and transitivity identifies them with each other. The standard-etale presentation and simple-root uniqueness argument remain in the imported theorem, so the unit route is preserved.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $(S,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let $\varphi:S\to B$ be a ring map such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is etale, and let $\mathfrak q'\subset B$ be a prime ideal with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')=\mathfrak m$ such that the induced map of residue fields $\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is bijective. If $\sigma,\tau:B\to S$ are $S$-algebra homomorphisms with $\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q'$ and $\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q'$, then $\sigma=\tau$.

proof.text: Since $S$ is henselian, simple roots modulo $\mathfrak m$ of monic polynomials over $S$ lift to roots in $S$. Let $x=\mathfrak q'\in\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $y=\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ its image. The scheme residue fields at $x$ and $y$ are $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ and $\kappa$, compatibly with $B\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ and $S\to\kappa$, so the residue-field map of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ at $x$ is the given map $\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$. The composite $S\to\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is surjective, so this residue-field map is surjective, and it is injective because it is a homomorphism of fields.

Apply the root-lifting retraction lemma to the $S$-algebra $B$ with this root-lifting property and this residue-field bijection. Both given algebra maps have maximal-ideal preimage $\mathfrak q'$, so its uniqueness clause identifies each with the unique retraction, and hence $\sigma=\tau$. ([lem-weil-pbc-root-lifting-etale-retraction]).
